junction.name: Lenox Avenue & West 125 Street, New York City

claims.text: Lenox Avenue & West 125 Street had 104 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 41 pedestrians injured, 29 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $7.1 million a year.
46% of crashes here had “driver inattention/distraction” recorded as a contributing factor, against 27% at the city's priority junctions.
27% of crashes here involved a two-wheeler, against 16% at the city's priority junctions.
13% of crashes here had a cyclist hurt, against 7% at the city's priority junctions.

Held up on later years: “driver inattention/distraction” was recorded in 44% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 26% at the city's priority junctions (found by the greedy search and the exhaustive search).

Held up on later years: a two-wheeler was involved in 28% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 16% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst and the greedy search and the exhaustive search).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 3.1 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $1.1 million a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 1.6 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $556,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Lenox Avenue, West 125 Street (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 9, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 10.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 9, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 10
Subject: Request for safety study at Lenox Avenue & West 125 Street

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

I am writing to request a safety study at the junction of Lenox Avenue & West 125 Street.

Over the 5 years from 31 October 2021, the official record at this junction shows 219 crashes, including 104 injury crashes. 41 pedestrians and 29 cyclists were injured, and no one was killed. This is a city priority location. The cost of harm is about $7.1 million per year in the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars). No recent safety work is recorded for this junction in this period. A Leading Pedestrian Interval signal was recorded in 2010.

Please review the following low-cost fixes on the roads you are responsible for:

On Lenox Avenue and West 125 Street, please consider longer yellow signal times. This is expected to prevent about 5.7 injury crashes per year, avoiding about $1,937,000 in harm per year. Please first check on site for an entry on yellow or red. It would pay for itself if works cost less than about $13.6 million.

On Lenox Avenue and West 125 Street, please consider reflective backplates on the traffic signals. This is expected to prevent about 3.1 injury crashes per year, avoiding about $1,068,000 in harm per year. Please first check on site for an entry on yellow or red. It would pay for itself if works cost less than about $7.5 million.

Thank you for your help.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
